messages:
Elaine H: Heads up — after the tokenizer upgrade on canary (hf/tokenizers 0.12.1 -> 0.13.0) we saw a large drop in prefix cache hit-rate for a subset of prompt templates. hit-rate went from ~68% -> ~41% on the top-50 routes. p50 latency +18ms, p95 +45ms. :grimacing:
Miguel R: ugh. did batching or kernel selection change too or just tokenization?
Elaine H: I double-checked deployment diff — serving runtime kernels unchanged. batching heuristics were identical. The only diffs are tokenizer and a small system-prompt tweak for tool-calls.
Sara L: do we have a reproducible sample? can we run the cache hit profiler on canary traffic?
Elaine H: yes ran a 10k sample locally and here are quick numbers: before: hit 6820/10000 (68.2%). after: hit 4120/10000 (41.2%). Many misses are short prefixes (first 8-30 tokens).
Zach P: interesting — short prefixes are more sensitive to tokenization changes because token boundaries shift a lot. any common token differences?
Miguel R: I dumped a diff set of tokenized prefixes. majority are because NBSP and non-ascii punctuation split differently, and sometimes the tokenizer emits a leading _ for certain punctuation which changes the hash.
Kevin M: can you paste an example?
Miguel R: sure:
```
# before (0.12.1) -> tokens
['▁Hello', '▁world', '!']
# after (0.13.0) -> tokens
['▁Hello', '▁world', '!', '▁']
```
That trailing token causes prefix mismatch when we compute fingerprint on raw token sequence.
Elaine H: thanks. so root cause is tokenization-induced prefix divergence. but we also saw kernel selection drifting on canary: slightly larger microbatches were chosen because queueing increased when hit-rate dropped, which nudged kernel selection to a different GEMM path for some layers — that amplified p95.
Sara L: oof the interaction between cache hit-rate and kernel path is subtle but real. fix options: 1) pin tokenizer version in the runtime environment (quick), 2) change cache key to use a canonical normalization + tokenizer-version tag, 3) smarter warmup to prefill likely short prefixes, 4) normalize system prompt & tool metadata before hashing.
Zach P: i like 2 + 4 as a long-term. include tokenizer version in key so different tokenizers don't collide but also canonicalize whitespace and invisible chars.
Miguel R: prototype normalization pipeline: trim, normalize NFKC, collapse whitespace (including NBSP -> space), remove tool-specific ephemeral fields from tool-call JSON (like "__client_time"). then hash tokens with: SHA1(token_bytes) + ":tok="+tokenizer_version.
Elaine H: example key pseudocode:
```
norm = normalize_prompt(raw_prompt)
toks = tokenizer.encode(norm)
fingerprint = sha1(toks)
cache_key = f"pf:{fingerprint}:tok={tokenizer.version}:sysv={sys_prompt_hash}"
```
where sys_prompt_hash changes only when system prompt meaningfully changes (not whitespace).
Kevin M: sysv is important — we shouldn't invalidate cache for benign formatting changes in system prompts. maybe compute sys_prompt_hash from the normalized semantic payload (strip comments/metadata).
Sara L: agree. also add a small TTL-stretch for recently evicted prefixes: when a prefix misses, spawn an async warmup for likely continuations (prefetch top-k continuations observed historically). this reduces the cold-start penalty.
Miguel R: did a quick warmup sim: prefetch top-3 completions for top-200 prefixes reduces observed p95 by ~12-15% in the replay. But warmup increases GPU cycles — need to weigh unit cost.
Elaine H: ops question: how to ship without risk? immediate step: pin tokenizer on canary back to 0.12.1 and enable logging for normalized keys + a sampling of raw/useful misses. then deploy key-change feature behind a flag for controlled rollout.
OpsBot: deploy/canary rolled back: canary-tokenizer -> pinned@0.12.1 by @Elaine H at 2026-03-18T18:32:10Z :white_check_mark:
Zach P: we should also add a small regression test in repo: take canonical prompt fixtures + multiple tokenizer versions and assert either key includes version or normalized tokens are identical within tolerance.
Kevin M: also add a perf regression monitor: track route-level cache-hit and if drop > 10% trigger an alert so we don't erode tail latency silently.
Sara L: question on storage: if we include tokenizer version in key, we'll have duplicate cached entries across versions — can increase storage but avoids cross-version collisions. acceptable tradeoff?
Elaine H: for short term yes. storage delta should be small since tokenization churn is rare. long term we can add canonicalization that reduces duplication.
Miguel R: i've opened a tiny RFC gist: https://gist.github.com/miguelr/prompt-fingerprint-proposal with normalization rules and example hashes.
Elaine H: action items:
- Miguel: land normalization util + unit tests (token diffs) behind feature flag — target EOD tomorrow
- Zach: add regression monitors & alert rules on route hit-rate — PT 1 day
- Kevin: add sys_prompt semantic hashing util and docs — PT 2 days
- Sara: prototype warmup prefetch sim on replay infra and cost analysis — PT 3 days
- Ops: keep tokenizer pinned on production until feature flag reaches 100%

Miguel R: started a small profiler run across 50k requests: `python -m infra.tools.cache_profiler --model redwood/llama-13b-v1 --sample 50000 --out /tmp/cprof.json` and storing token diff stats. first results show top mismatches are NBSP, em-dash, and JSON tool-field ordering.
Zach P: re ordering — canonicalize JSON fields for tool calls (sort keys) before hashing. that should remove a lot of noisy misses.
Elaine H: thanks team. labeling this thread as action/needs-followup. will post a short postmortem once we have numbers post-rollout. :eyes:
OpsBot: reminder: automated canary metrics dashboard created: https://redwood-infra.internal/dash/canary-cachekey (view-only)
Sara L: also note: we should update docs for "cache key hygiene" in eng-runtime README so new models/tokenizers follow the pattern. tiny PR incoming. :sparkles:
Kevin M: tl;dr: tokenizer drift caused token boundary shifts -> prefix fingerprint mismatch -> lower cache hit -> more queuing -> different kernel path -> worse tail latency. multi-pronged fix: pin, normalize, version-tag keys, warmup, alerts.
